About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India's full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role

Engagement Manager is a senior client-facing role in the vertical. You own pipeline development, account strategy, and long-term engagement management. This is a builder role for someone who understands the procurement landscape, can engage at the CXO and technical leadership level, and can convert complex AI capability into funded, deployable programmes.

What You'll Do

• Own the day-to-day management of active client engagements, from scoping and alignment through to operational handover and adoption

• Serve as the primary point of contact for clients across the engagement lifecycle; manage expectations proactively and honestly

• Translate client operational problems into precise briefs that deployment and engineering teams can act on

• Track delivery against commitments; surface risks early and drive resolution without waiting for escalation

• Work with Strategic Deployment Engineers to ensure what is being built reflects what the client actually needs

• Support pipeline development: account mapping, stakeholder outreach, and PoC scoping

• Build and maintain working relationships with mid-to-senior client stakeholders; grow account depth over time

• Surface ground-level observations back to the vertical as market intelligence

What We're Looking For

• 4–6 years of professional experience; foundational background at a top-tier consulting firm strongly preferred — with a track record of owning complex analytical work, structuring ambiguous problems, and being accountable for outcomes

• At least 2 years in strategic or complex enterprise GTM, account management, or programme delivery — where you owned client relationships, not just supported them

• Comfort operating in long-cycle, relationship-driven environments where trust is built over months, not deals

• Strong written and verbal communication, able to hold a room with senior stakeholders and write briefs that people act on

• Familiarity with GenAI or ML concepts sufficient to engage credibly with technical teams and translate capability to clients

• Experience in or adjacent to defence, government, critical infrastructure and complex enterprises is a plus

Signals We Look For

• You've owned something - a client, a mandate - and driven it to a conclusion without being

managed to do it

• You've had to deliver a hard message to a client or stakeholder, done it early, and held the

relationship

• You think in structures. You make complex problems legible and actionable for the people who

need to move on them

• You've worked across functions — engineering, finance, policy, or operations — and made thing happen without formal authority

• Experience at a top-tier consulting firm; owning complex analytical problem-solving, structuring ambiguous mandates, and being accountable for outcomes is strongly valued.

Who You Are

• You treat client ownership as a baseline, not a virtue — if the engagement is in trouble, it's your problem to fix

• You are direct; you say what you actually think, including to people more senior than you

• You are comfortable with ambiguity and genuinely energised by environments where the answer isn't obvious

• You move with urgency and bring others with you through influence, not authority

Why Sarvam?

Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems that push the frontiers of AI with real population-scale impact.

• Work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar

• High ownership and high impact, from day one

• Everything we do is AI-first, from the way we build and ship to the way we think about problems

• You can work on problems that could change how an entire country learns, works, and communicates

If you want to work on problems at the frontier of AI in India, Sarvam is the place to be.

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. About the Role

This is an intellectually demanding role. The Data Scientist anchors the evaluations function for this vertical — designing, building, and maintaining evaluation frameworks that measure model and system quality in operational context. You are not running standard benchmarks. You are building domain-specific eval harnesses for high-stakes use cases where a wrong answer carries real consequences.

You will work closely with the MLOps Engineer, the PM, and the deployment team. The evaluations you design are the mechanism by which the team determines whether what we've built is good enough to deploy — and whether it stays good after deployment.

What You'll Do

• Design and build evaluation frameworks for Sarvam's AI outputs across domain-specific requirements: document comprehension, command summarisation, geospatial reasoning, enterprise workflow automation, and others as they emerge

• Define quality metrics in collaboration with domain experts and clients; translate operational requirements into measurable, defensible signals

• Run structured evaluation cycles pre- and post-deployment; build dashboards that surface model quality in production

• Identify failure modes, edge cases, and distribution shifts — with the bias of someone looking for what's wrong, not confirming what's right

• Collaborate with the MLOps Engineer to operationalise eval pipelines — automated, triggered by deployment events, versioned, and reproducible

• Build and manage domain-specific datasets for fine-tuning, evaluation, and benchmarking — including human annotation workflows where needed

• Publish internal findings and quality reports that feed the product and engineering roadmap

What We're Looking For

• 3–6 years in data science, ML research, or applied AI; at least 2 years working with LLMs in production contexts

• Strong statistics and probability fundamentals — you understand what makes an evaluation valid and what makes it misleading

• Experience designing evaluation frameworks from scratch: custom metrics, inter-rater reliability, red-teaming methodologies

• Python proficiency; comfort with pandas, NumPy, HuggingFace datasets, RAGAS, EleutherAI Eval Harness, LangSmith, or equivalent

• Experience with prompt engineering, model fine-tuning, or RLHF in applied settings

• Ability to work with unstructured domain data: PDFs, doctrine documents, transcripts, and field reports

Bonus Points

• Prior work in high-stakes domains (healthcare, legal, defence, finance) where output quality carries real-world consequences

• Red-teaming or adversarial evaluation experience

match every line of this specification. If this problem excites you and you believe you can do this work, we want to hear from you.

About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India's full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role

Embedded Data Scientists transform complex client data into structures that AI systems can reliably reason over. You are deployed alongside Strategic Deployment Engineers at client sites, working directly with client data environments to understand, structure, and operationalise large-scale datasets.

This means working with heterogeneous, multimodal data — including documents, images, audio, geospatial data, and structured records — and designing the semantic structures that allow AI systems to interpret and reason over that data.

You will define how data is represented inside the AI system: how documents are segmented, how metadata is defined, how entities and relationships are represented, and how different data modalities connect. You will design ontologies, tagging systems, and knowledge graph structures that allow the reasoning engine to operate effectively.

You will often work with classified or operationally sensitive datasets in environments where standard tooling may not exist. You will own the quality of the data layer in your assigned accounts, ensuring the system is built on a foundation that enables reliable reasoning at scale.

What You'll Do

• Understand the client's data landscape across documents, imagery, audio, geospatial data, and structured records — including data sources, formats, workflows, and domain terminology

• Design domain ontologies representing entities, relationships, hierarchies, and operational concepts within the client's data environment

• Define document segmentation and chunking strategies that preserve semantic meaning and support effective retrieval

• Work with heterogeneous datasets and define how different modalities should be indexed, embedded, and linked

• Collaborate with Strategic Deployment Engineers to translate semantic structures into operational data ingestion pipelines

• Evaluate how well the AI system retrieves and reasons over client data, and refine structures to improve performance

• Collaborate with the models and other teams to define benchmarks and evaluation criteria that reflect real-world deployment conditions

• Translate insights from client data environments into structured signals for product and engineering teams

What We're Looking For

• 2–5 years in data science, applied machine learning, or large-scale data analysis roles

• Strong Python skills including pandas, NumPy, and modern NLP or LLM tooling

• Solid grounding in ML fundamentals — enough to understand model behaviour, contribute to evaluation design, and collaborate with a models team on training and benchmarking

• Experience working with large unstructured datasets including documents, transcripts, reports, or operational records

• Familiarity with LLM-based systems, retrieval pipelines, or vector search systems

• Experience designing or working with data schemas, metadata frameworks, entity models, or semantic data structures

Signals We Look For

• You've worked with real-world, messy, unstructured data and built something rigorous from it

• You are comfortable designing structure where none exists — defining schemas, ontologies, and metadata frameworks from scratch

• You can translate complex data insights into explanations that engineers and client stakeholders can act on

Who You Are

• You are comfortable operating with autonomy in client environments; you don't need a data team around you to do rigorous work

• You move fluently between domain understanding, data modelling, and AI system design

• You move between the technical and the operational: you understand what the data means in the context of what operators actually do with it

Bonus Points

• Familiarity with knowledge graphs, ontologies, or semantic data modelling

• Experience with multimodal datasets (text, imagery, audio, geospatial, or structured data)

• Experience operating in constrained or air-gapped environments

Why Sarvam?

Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems that push the frontiers of AI with real population-scale impact.

• Work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar

• High ownership and high impact, from day one

• Everything we do is AI-first, from the way we build and ship to the way we think about problems

• You can work on problems that could change how an entire country learns, works, and communicates

If you want to work on problems at the frontier of AI in India, Sarvam is the place to be.

About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India's full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role

Embedded Infrastructure Engineers design, build, and maintain the data infrastructure that underpins AI system deployments at client sites. You work alongside Embedded Data Scientists and Strategic Deployment Engineers to ensure that terabyte-scale datasets can be ingested, stored, queried, and served to AI reasoning engines reliably and performantly.

This means building and operating data platforms that handle terabyte-scale persistent data stores and sustained large daily ingestion volumes across structured records, documents, imagery, audio, and geospatial data. You will design and maintain the databases, object stores, ingestion pipelines, and processing layers that make this possible.

You will make critical decisions about storage architecture, indexing strategies, pipeline orchestration, and system performance — often in constrained, air-gapped, or operationally sensitive environments where you cannot rely on managed cloud services or standard enterprise tooling. You will own the reliability and performance of the infrastructure layer in your assigned accounts.

What You'll Do

• Design and operate data storage architectures (relational, document, vector, object storage) capable of managing terabyte-scale datasets across multiple modalities

• Build and maintain ingestion pipelines that reliably process daily data influx — including batch and streaming workloads — with monitoring, error handling, and backpressure management

• Implement indexing, partitioning, and query optimisation strategies that allow AI systems and data scientists to retrieve and reason over large datasets with acceptable latency

• Work with Embedded Data Scientists to translate ontologies, schemas, and semantic structures into performant physical data models and storage configurations

• Deploy and manage database systems, vector stores, and search infrastructure in air-gapped, on-premise, or security-constrained environments

• Build observability into the data platform: monitor pipeline health, storage utilisation, query performance, and ingestion lag

• Own capacity planning and scaling decisions for data infrastructure across assigned client deployments

• Collaborate with product and engineering teams to feed infrastructure learnings back into the core platform and tooling

What We're Looking For

• 4–8 years in data infrastructure, data engineering, platform engineering, or site reliability engineering, ideally at organisations operating at significant data scale

• Direct experience managing multi-terabyte data stores — you have personally built or operated systems handling 10TB+ of persistent data and sustained high-throughput ingestion

• Deep working knowledge of at least two of: PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Elasticsearch, ClickHouse, or comparable systems — including tuning, indexing, partitioning, and operational management

• Experience building production data ingestion pipelines using Apache Kafka, Apache Spark, Airflow, Flink, dbt, or equivalent frameworks

• Strong proficiency in Python and/or Go, with experience writing production infrastructure tooling and automation

• Solid understanding of storage systems and formats: object storage (S3/MinIO), columnar formats (Parquet, ORC), and how to choose the right storage layer for the workload

• Familiarity with containerisation and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes) in production settings

• Experience with infrastructure-as-code and deployment automation (Terraform or similar)

Bonus Points

• Experience with vector databases or embedding stores (Milvus, Weaviate, Qdrant, pgvector, or similar)

• Experience deploying and operating infrastructure in air-gapped, on-premise, or hybrid environments

you believe you can do this work; we want to hear from you.

About the Role

We're looking for product managers who are builders first — people who talk to customers constantly, ship real product to real users, and get into the details of how AI systems behave in production. This is not a role tied to one specific product line. Based on your strengths and interests, you could work across consumer AI products, enterprise platforms, developer tools, speech and voice systems, or edge deployments.

What You'll Do

• Own a product area end-to-end — talk to users, write specs, define success metrics, ship, and measure outcomes

• Get into the details of how AI systems behave in production: prompt design, model selection, latency budgets, failure modes, and eval pipelines

• Write code, prompts, and copy when that's the fastest path to learning or validating an idea

• Set up funnels, write queries, and instrument events to diagnose what's working and what's broken

• Work directly with engineering, design, and leadership — no layers, no hand-offs

• Ship product every week, not plans

 

What We're Looking For

• 3–7 years of product management experience; you have shipped real products at meaningful scale at strong B2C or B2B companies in India

• Currently a product manager — this role is not for people transitioning from consulting, project management, or program management

• Hands-on familiarity with AI: you've built agents, understand how context windows work, and have thought through trade-offs like cost vs. latency vs. accuracy — experience with evals, tool calling, or agentic workflows is a strong plus

• Strong data skills: comfortable writing SQL, setting up funnels from scratch in PostHog, Mixpanel, or similar tools, and defining meaningful success metrics (not vanity numbers)

• Strong product thinking: you start with the customer's problem, talk to users regularly, can structure vague problem spaces, and ship v1 without over-engineering

• Systems thinker: you see the handshakes between components, the failure modes, and the dependencies when you look at a product

• High ownership, high agency: you don't wait for permission, you solve problems, and you've stayed up to fix something because you couldn't let it stay broken

• Clear communicator: you can explain complex technical concepts simply — to engineers, leadership, and users alike

 

Bonus Points

• You've built at least one working AI agent end-to-end — not a demo, something that actually does a job

• You've used tools like Claude Code, built skills, or set up agentic workflows, and have opinions on when to use agents vs. simpler approaches

• You have side projects, open-source contributions, or products shipped outside of work

• You can point to 2–3 things in your life — product or otherwise — where you went deep and had real impact

 

Why Sarvam?

Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems that push the frontiers of AI with real population-scale impact.

• High ownership and high impact, from day one

• Everything we do is AI-first, from the way we build and ship to the way we think about problems

• You can work on problems that could change how an entire country learns, works, and communicates

If you want to work on problems at the frontier of AI in India, Sarvam is the place to be.

About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India's full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

 

About the Role

These are not form-and-table frontend roles. The frontend engineers on this team build the interfaces that sit on top of Sarvam's AI stack in some of the most demanding environments in the country. You will own the frontend layer of multiple 'atoms' — replicable, deployable product components — and work closely with backend engineers, the PM, and the deployment team. These interfaces must work in offline-first, low-bandwidth, hardened client environments, not just on a MacBook over broadband.

 

What You'll Do

• Design and build performant, production-grade frontend interfaces for strategic sector and enterprise AI use cases: geospatial overlays, simulation UIs, natural language access layers, ontology viewers, data ingestion dashboards, and complex enterprise workflows

• Own the frontend layer of atoms end-to-end — from component architecture to deployment in client-embedded environments

• Collaborate with backend engineers and the PM to ship complete, scoped atoms into the hands of real users

• Build for constrained environments: offline-first, low-bandwidth, limited hardware — not the idealised development environment

• Contribute to shared frontend infrastructure: component libraries, design system, and state management patterns

• Participate in field testing and client feedback loops with Strategic Deployment Engineers across strategic sector and complex enterprise accounts

 

What We're Looking For

• 3–6 years in frontend engineering with shipped, production-grade products

• Deep React proficiency; TypeScript; modern CSS (Tailwind or equivalent); strong component architecture instincts

• State management proficiency: Zustand, Redux Toolkit, or equivalent; strong async data patterns

• Data visualisation experience: D3.js, Mapbox/Leaflet, Deck.gl for geospatial, Recharts, or equivalent — at least one in production

• REST and WebSocket API integration; sufficient backend awareness to debug across the boundary

• Performance engineering: bundle optimisation, lazy loading, and rendering performance in low-resource environments

 

Bonus Points

• WebGL or Three.js for 3D visualisation

• Electron or desktop app experience

• Offline-first or PWA architecture

• Prior work on dashboards, command-and-control UIs, or complex enterprise tooling

Note: We are looking for people who can own the outcomes described here, not people who

match every line of this specification. If this problem excites you and you believe you can do this work, we want to hear from you.

 

Why Sarvam?

Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems that push the frontiers of AI with real population-scale impact.

• Work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar

• High ownership and high impact, from day one

• Everything we do is AI-first, from the way we build and ship to the way we think about problems

• You can work on problems that could change how an entire country learns, works, and communicates

If you want to work on problems at the frontier of AI in India, Sarvam is the place to be.

Ship the best design work of your career.

 

Design at Sarvam has had an outsized impact on everything we've built so far, and we're now growing the team. We care deeply about design, both the craft and science of it and we're looking to build a world class design team. We're looking for designers who treat design as the core of the product, not a layer applied at the end.



What we're looking for

  • 4+ years designing digital products end to end at a product-driven company

  • Design product concepts that balance vision, craft, speed, and business value.

  • A portfolio that shows real craft. Typography, hierarchy, motion, interaction, the full stack of visual and UX thinking

  • Strong UX intuition. You can take abstract ideas and turn them into flows people understand without thinking

  • Strong product judgment. You think about activation, engagement, and retention as design problems

  • Range across UX, UI, interaction, and systems

  • A bias for shipping. You'd rather ship at 80% and learn than polish in private for three weeks

  • Comfort with ambiguity and ownership. You don't wait to be told what to do

  • Strong opinions, loosely held. You argue your case and update when you're wrong


Design systems

You know when to use the system, when to break it, and when to evolve it. You've built or maintained one before and understand what it takes to keep it alive.

Strong plus

  • You already work like an AI-native designer. Claude Code and Cursor are part of how you think, prototype, and ship. You can hold a real conversation about MCP, skills, frontend constraints, and how to set up a design system so AI tools actually work with it

  • You're data curious. You've lived in Mixpanel or PostHog, can read a funnel, and can write SQL well enough to answer your own product questions.
    What's in it for you

What's in it for you

  1. A place to genuinely spread your wings. Room to experiment and be okay with failure.

  2. Work with some of the best design talent in India. Check out sarvam.ai/brand to get a sense of where the bar is.

  3. A place to be ambitious. We want to push the bar on design and set global benchmarks.

  4. High ownership. You pick problems, own them end to end, and yes, you ship to prod. You have access to Mixpanel, customers, engineering codebase.

  5. Build for India. You design for a billion people across languages and contexts most global teams never have to think about.

About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India's full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role

The Solution Architect is the trusted technical advisor who bridges what Sarvam builds and what the client needs. You will work alongside the sales and GTM team to understand prospect requirements, translate them into compelling technical narratives, and ensure every deal moves forward with clarity and momentum. You own the technical relationship with the customer's technology decision maker, end-to-end through the pre-sales cycle.

This is not a support role. You will be in client meetings from day one, shaping how enterprises understand and evaluate Sarvam's AI platform. You will build demos, craft proposals, run pilots, and work directly with product and engineering teams to close the gap between what a client asks for and what Sarvam can deliver. The problems you work on will span voice AI, document intelligence, multilingual agents, and enterprise-grade API platforms.

If you are someone who can hold a technical conversation with an engineering lead and a business conversation with a CXO in the same meeting, this role is for you.

What You'll Do

  • Own the pre-sales cycle for assigned accounts: from discovery and qualification through to technical proposal and pilot design

  • Build and deliver compelling product demos tailored to each prospect's industry, use case, and technical environment

  • Create proposals, RFP/RFI responses, solution architecture documents, and commercial models in collaboration with the sales lead

  • Work with Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSEs) and product teams to scope technical feasibility and define pilot success criteria

  • Develop a deep understanding of Sarvam's full product stack: Samvaad, Studio, Akshar, and the API platform (TTS, STT, document digitisation)

  • Build reusable demos, case studies, battlecards, and proposal templates that scale across accounts and lift the rest of the team

  • Track and communicate client feedback and feature gaps back to product teams with clarity and context

  • Support deal reviews and pipeline discussions with data, timelines, and risk flags

What We're Looking For

  • 3-5 years in a pre-sales, solutions consulting, technical sales, or product-facing GTM role, ideally in B2B SaaS or enterprise technology

  • Strong communication skills: you can explain complex technical products in simple, outcome-oriented language

  • Comfort with technical concepts: APIs, cloud infrastructure, AI/ML workflows. You don't need to write code, but you need to understand how systems connect

  • Experience building proposals, decks, or solution documents for enterprise buyers

  • High attention to detail: proposals go out clean, demos run without surprises, timelines are tracked

  • Willingness to learn fast and go deep on Sarvam's product and technology stack

Bonus Points

  • Prior exposure to AI/ML products, conversational AI, or language technology

  • Experience working with Indian enterprise or government clients

  • Familiarity with Indian language ecosystems and the specific challenges of multilingual AI deployment

  • Background in consulting, business analysis, or solutions engineering

Note: We are looking for people who can own the outcomes described here, not people who match every line of this specification. If this problem excites you and you believe you can do this work, we want to hear from you.

Why Sarvam?

Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems that push the frontiers of AI with real population-scale impact.

  • Work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar

  • High ownership and high impact, from day one

  • Everything we do is AI-first, from the way we build and ship to the way we think about problems

  • You can work on problems that could change how an entire country learns, works, and communicates

If you want to work on problems at the frontier of AI in India, Sarvam is the place to be.

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The Role

At the heart of Sarvam’s conversational AI platform sits the system that lets our customers build, configure, deploy, and operate voice agents and campaigns — at scale. Today it handles 50M+ minutes of conversations every month, and it’s growing fast.

We’re looking for a Staff Engineer to own this system end-to-end. The data model. The APIs. The orchestration. The reliability. The performance. The standards we hold ourselves to. This is an IC role with the scope and authority of one — no people management, just the systems and the bar.

What You’ll Own

• The end-to-end backend for agent, campaign, and user management — from data modeling through API design to deployment, in Python and FastAPI

• Workflow orchestration with Temporal for complex, long-running, stateful operations

• Performance and reliability for a multi-tenant SaaS platform operating at sub-second latency SLOs

• Observability — logging, metrics, tracing — so the team can debug production confidently and quickly

• Integration testing — the test infrastructure that lets us ship fast without breaking customer-facing systems

• Close collaboration with the frontend team (Next.js) to deliver an experience worthy of the underlying platform

• Setting the design-first and documentation-first engineering culture within your team — RFCs before code, decisions written down, no tribal knowledge

What We’re Looking For

• 5–10 years building production backend systems, with deep expertise in Python and FastAPI (or Golang)

• A track record of full-stack ownership — you’ve designed systems end-to-end, made the trade-offs, and operated them in production

• Hands-on experience with workflow orchestration at scale, ideally Temporal

• Built and operated high-scale distributed systems — multi-tenant, low-latency, resilient under real load

• Strong PostgreSQL and Redis fundamentals — schema design, query performance, caching strategy

• The judgment to know when to build vs. buy, when to optimize vs. ship, when to abstract vs. inline

Nice to Have

• Experience building products on top of LLMs or AI/ML systems

• Background in telephony, VoIP, or SIP infrastructure

• Time at an early- or growth-stage startup — comfort with ambiguity, speed, and ownership

The company is developing India’s full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India’s leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role

Sarvam's model APIs (ASR, TTS, Vision, LLM, Translate) are how developers and enterprises ship products on our foundation models. The platform handles tens of millions of API calls every day, over HTTP and WebSockets, with metering, billing, prepaid wallets, and rate-limiting all part of the same stack. Today it's FastAPI and Python; we're in the middle of rewriting it in Go.

We're hiring a Staff Engineer to own this platform end-to-end. The architecture. The reliability. The performance. The standards. This is an IC role.

What You’ll Do

  • The end-to-end design and evolution of the platform, from the moment a request hits the edge to the response that goes back out

  • The Python→Go rewrite: leading the architecture, setting the patterns, and bringing the platform across without compromising reliability

  • Audio pipeline engineering: TTS chunking around model context limits, sample-rate adjustments and format encoding, VAD-based silence detection for ASR

  • Vision pipelines: orchestrating OCR, layout detection, and VLM harnesses for structured data extraction

  • Streaming infrastructure: WebSocket connections, queue-based batch processing, back pressure, low-latency model invocation

  • The commercial layer: metering, billing, prepaid wallet management, and rate-limiting, engineered to the same bar as the model APIs themselves

  • Performance and reliability for a multi-tenant platform operating at sub-second latency SLOs

  • Observability (logging, metrics, tracing), so the team can debug production confidently and quickly

  • Integration testing infrastructure: the harness that lets us ship fast without breaking customer-facing APIs

  • Close partnership with the Inference and MLOps teams, mentoring them on production engineering so model serving is fast, reliable, and operable

  • Design-first, documentation-first engineering culture within the team: RFCs before code, decisions written down, no tribal knowledge

What We’re Looking For

  • 7+ years building production backend systems at scale

  • Strong Go in production: you've designed, built, and operated Go services under real load

  • Comfortable in Python: you'll work in both languages through the rewrite, and FastAPI is the current foundation

  • A track record of designing and operating high-scale, low-latency, multi-tenant distributed systems

  • Hands-on experience with real-time / streaming systems: WebSockets, long-lived connections, backpressure

  • Strong PostgreSQL and Redis fundamentals: schema design, query performance, caching strategy

  • Comfort running services on Kubernetes in production

  • The judgment of a senior IC: when to build vs. buy, when to optimize vs. ship, when to abstract vs. inline, and how to bring others up with you

Bonus Points

  • Experience serving LLMs, ASR, TTS, or vision models in production

  • Background in audio processing (pyav, FFmpeg, codec / sample-rate work, VAD)

  • Experience building metering, billing, or wallet / payments infrastructure

  • Time at an early- or growth-stage startup: comfort with ambiguity, speed, and ownership

If you want to work on problems at the frontier of AI in India, Sarvam is the place to be.

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. About the Role

Sarvam runs a large, multi-vendor GPU fleet that serves two demanding workloads on the same physical infrastructure: training jobs that span hundreds of GPUs and must run uninterrupted for weeks, and inference services that must hold a flat p99 under production load. Keeping both healthy at once is a hard, specialized reliability problem, and it is the problem this team exists to solve.

This is not a Kubernetes administration role. We assume Kubernetes fluency as a baseline. The difficulty lies above and below it - in parallel filesystems under heavy checkpoint load, in RDMA fabrics that degrade quietly, in NCCL hangs whose root cause may be the network or the kernel, in driver and firmware drift across heterogeneous hardware, and in distributed training failures that masquerade as infrastructure faults.

We are hiring a team of specialists rather than a set of identical generalists. This posting covers five areas of focus. We expect candidates to bring genuine depth in one and working fluency across the others, because on a shared fleet a storage problem often first appears as a training hang, and the engineer on call must route an incident correctly before anyone can resolve it.

When you apply, please indicate the area of focus that best matches your experience. Strong generalists are welcome; we will place you where your depth is most useful.

What You’ll Do

  • Operate the GPU fleet end to end across training and serving - provisioning, observability, capacity, and fleet health.

  • Hold a meaningful on-call rotation, write runbooks that hold up under pressure, and drive postmortems that produce durable fixes.

  • Build the internal tooling the team relies on, rather than operating off-the-shelf systems alone.

  • Partner with ML and platform teams to keep large runs alive and serving latency predictable.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years in infrastructure or site reliability engineering, including 2+ years operating GPU clusters at scale.*

  • Demonstrated on-call ownership of infrastructure that mattered, with a track record of postmortems that led to real change.

  • Proficiency in Python or Go, used to build and maintain internal tooling.

  • Working fluency across all five areas of focus below - enough to recognize, triage, and route a problem outside your specialty, even if the fix belongs to a teammate.

* For the Storage and Fabric areas of focus, we will weigh deep domain expertise against the GPU-cluster requirement; exceptional specialists with less direct GPU-fleet time are encouraged to apply.

Bring depth in one of the five areas below; expect to be conversational across the rest.

  1. Distributed high-performance storage — operate a parallel filesystem (Lustre, GPFS, WEKA, or BeeGFS) at scale and keep it from stalling under checkpoint-write storms.

  2. Fabric & RDMA networking — InfiniBand or RoCE health, NVLink/NVSwitch topology, and RDMA debugging that catches degradation before the workload feels it.

  3. GPU systems reliability — NCCL debugging, driver and firmware lifecycle across a mixed fleet, and DCGM-based node health at scale.

  4. Kubernetes platform reliability — the GPU operator stack, scheduling (Slurm-on-k8s or pure k8s), multi-tenant isolation, and cost/SLO primitives.

  5. Training & inference workload reliability — hang and straggler detection, checkpoint/restart, and protecting serving p99 with HA and DR.

Bonus Points

  • Slurm and Kubernetes hybrid environments.

  • On-premise GPU deployment, including coordination with datacenter operations on power, cooling, and InfiniBand cabling.

  • Experience with Indian NCPs, DGX SuperPOD, Lambda, CoreWeave, NeevCloud etc.

  • Multi-tenant GPU isolation (MIG, MPS, time-slicing) in production.

Platform Engineer - AI Infrastructure

About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India’s full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India’s leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role

Sarvam runs a large, multi-vendor GPU fleet that serves two demanding workloads on the same physical infrastructure: training jobs that span hundreds of GPUs, and inference services that must hold a flat p99 under production load. This role builds the platform that sits on top of that fleet - the scheduling, scaling, multi-tenancy, serving, and self-service layers that let our ML teams use thousands of GPUs without a human in the loop for every job.

This is the build side of infrastructure, not the operate side. Our SREs keep the fleet reliable and carry the pager; you build the systems that make the fleet usable - and that make it break less in the first place. The work is heavy software engineering: you will design and ship control-plane services, scheduler integrations, autoscaling controllers, the inference-serving platform, RBAC and quota systems, observability and cost tooling, and the CLI and APIs ML engineers touch every day. You will treat the platform as a product and its internal users as customers.

You should be a strong systems engineer who is fluent in Kubernetes at the controller and internals level, comfortable in Go or Python, and literate in the GPU-specific constraints - MIG and GPU sharing, gang scheduling, topology-aware placement, RDMA - that make this different from a generic cloud platform.

What You’ll Do

This is the surface area of the platform. You won't own all of it at once - you'll take a capability and build it end to end - but you should be excited by most of it.

  • The serving platform. The control plane that turns a model artifact into a scalable, multi-tenant endpoint: intelligent routing and load balancing across replicas, rollout machinery (canary, blue-green, rollback), traffic splitting, model-version integration etc.

  • The scaling and elasticity layer. Autoscaling for both training (elastic and gang scaling, scale-to-fit) and serving (queue-depth and utilization-driven), capacity pooling across clusters, burst handling, preemption and reclaim, and efficient bin-packing across GPUs etc.

  • Scheduling and orchestration. The scheduler layer itself - Kueue, Volcano, Slurm-on-Kubernetes, or custom controllers - with gang scheduling, priority and preemption, queue fairness, quota enforcement, and topology-aware placement that keeps a job's ranks on the same fabric island.

  • Multi-tenancy, RBAC, and isolation. The tenant model and namespacing, RBAC and policy, quota and fair-share enforcement, MIG / MPS / time-slicing exposed as self-service tiers, secrets and credential management, and audit logging.

  • Networking components. Platform-level network plumbing - CNI configuration and custom components, ingress and service routing, RDMA / SR-IOV exposure into pods, tenant network policy and segmentation, and multi-cluster connectivity.

  • Observability and cost tooling. The metrics, logging, and tracing pipeline as a platform feature with cardinality managed at fleet scale.

  • The storage and data path. Abstractions over the parallel filesystem, caching tiers, volume provisioning, and data-locality-aware placement.

  • Developer experience and self-service. The layer ML engineers actually touch - CLI, SDK, and APIs, job-submission abstractions and inner-loop tooling.

  • Provisioning and infrastructure-as-code. The control plane that stands clusters up reproducibly - Terraform, Crossplane, or operators; node lifecycle and image management; driver and firmware rollout automation; and multi-vendor cluster bring-up.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years building infrastructure or platform software, with a track record of systems you designed and shipped - not scripts and glue, but services and control planes that others built on.

  • Strong software engineering in Go or Python, with the judgment to build maintainable systems and the depth to debug them in production.

  • Kubernetes at the controller and internals level - you have written operators or controllers, understand the scheduler and API machinery, and know where its abstractions leak.

  • Working literacy in the GPU-specific platform constraints: MIG and GPU sharing, gang scheduling, topology- and fabric-aware placement, and why training and serving contend for the same hardware.

  • A product mindset toward internal users - you design APIs and abstractions people want to use, and you measure the platform by adoption and self-service, not by tickets closed.

  • The range to own a capability end to end, from design through rollout to the documentation that makes it self-serve.

Bonus Points

  • Having built a serving or inference or training platform - routing, autoscaling, and rollout for model endpoints at scale, fine-tuning as a service etc.

  • Experience with GPU scheduling systems (Kueue, Volcano, Slurm, Run:ai, or custom schedulers) in multi-tenant production.

  • Multi-tenant isolation (MIG, MPS, time-slicing) shipped as a self-service platform capability rather than a one-off configuration.

  • Deep Kubernetes networking - CNI internals, custom network components, or RDMA / SR-IOV in pods.

  • On-premise GPU platform work, including multi-vendor or Indian NCP environments.

  • Open-source contributions to Kubernetes, scheduling, or GPU-platform projects.

About the Role

The Marketing Operations Manager makes Sarvam's marketing engine run. This role owns the systems, data, and processes that connect every campaign, channel, and team, from the website and developer signups through to pipeline and revenue. The job is to make marketing measurable: to know what is working, what is not, and where every rupee and hour is going. This person sits at the centre of a fast-moving marketing team spanning growth, demand generation, product marketing, and developer relations.   • Martech stack ownership. Own selection, integration, and administration of the marketing stack - CRM, marketing automation, analytics, attribution, and enrichment tools. Keep systems connected and data flowing cleanly between them.

  • Funnel instrumentation. Instrument the full funnel from first visit and developer signup through to MQL, SQL, and closed revenue. Define the stages, the data model, and the definitions everyone agrees on.

  • Attribution & reporting. Build and maintain attribution models and reporting that show what drives pipeline and usage. Deliver dashboards leadership actually uses to make decisions.

  • Lead management & routing. Own lead scoring, routing, and the MQL-to-SQL handoff with Sales, with clear SLAs on quality and follow-up. Keep the bridge between Marketing and Sales clean and accountable.

  • Data hygiene & governance. Keep the database accurate, deduplicated, and compliant. Own segmentation, list management, and data governance including consent and privacy requirements.

  • Process & enablement. Document workflows, build playbooks, and train the team on the systems. Remove the manual, repetitive work that slows the team down.

  • AI-native workflows. Use AI to compress every operational cycle — reporting, QA, enrichment, segmentation, and content ops. Treat the ops function itself as a place to apply Sarvam's own tools.

  • Budget & vendor management. Track marketing spend against pipeline, manage tool contracts and renewals, and surface where budget is and is not paying off.

  • 4-6 years in marketing operations, revenue operations, or a closely related role at a B2B technology or SaaS company

  • Hands-on expertise with at least one major marketing automation platform (HubSpot, Marketo, or similar) and a CRM (Salesforce or similar), including building workflows, scoring, and integrations yourself

  • Strong analytical capability - you build your own dashboards, define attribution, and pull and model your own data

  • Track record of designing and improving lead management, funnel instrumentation, and Marketing-to-Sales handoff processe

Location: Bengaluru

About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. We're looking for an HR Business Partner & Operations to be a strategic and hands-on partner to our business leaders. Business Partnering

  • Partner closely with business and function leaders to understand their goals and translate them into HR strategies and structures that support scale.

  • Advise on organizational design, performance management, and career development as teams grow.

  • Act as a trusted advisor and change agent through periods of organizational transformation and rapid growth.

  • Address employee relations matters, lead investigations where needed, and resolve conflicts fairly and swiftly.

People Operations & HR Systems

  • Own and continuously improve core HR processes across the employee lifecycle — onboarding, performance cycles, transfers, and exits.

  • Identify, evaluate, and implement HRMS tools for employee data, compensation, and performance management, ensuring the stack scales cleanly with headcount growth.

  • Ensure HR policies, labor law compliance, and documentation are current, consistent, and audit-ready.

  • Support compensation and benefits administration, including data accuracy, benchmarking inputs, and cycle execution.

  • Maintain and improve HR systems, dashboards, and reporting to give leadership clean, timely people data.

  • Support talent acquisition through workforce planning inputs and candidate evaluation where needed.

Culture & Engagement

  • Drive employee engagement, retention, and development initiatives that fit a fast paced, high-growth, tech-first environment.

  • Champion a high performance, high trust culture aligned with Sarvam's mission and pace.

Requirements

  • Degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field.

  • 5–8 years of HR experience, with at least 4 years in an HRBP, People Operations, or similar generalist role.

  • Hands-on experience in implementing HRMS/HRIS platforms (e.g., Darwinbox, Keka, Rippling, Lattice or similar) is strongly preferred.

  • Strong grounding in HR compliance, and process design.

  • Comfortable owning both strategic conversations with leaders and the operational details that make HR systems and processes work reliably.

  • Strong stakeholder management, communication, and problem-solving skills.

  • Thrives in a fast paced, high growth, ambiguity tolerant environment: startup or scale-up experience is a plus.

Why Sarvam?

  • Sarvam is a fast moving, high talent density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems that push the frontiers of AI with real population scale impact.

  • Work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar.

  • High impact, high agency role shaping HR strategy and systems from the ground up at a fast scaling AI company.

  • Be part of a mission driven team building India's sovereign AI stack, with exposure to a wide range of HR challenges, from strategy to systems.

 

If you’re passionate about shaping the people agenda in a mission first, cutting edge AI company, we’d love to hear from you!

Performance Engineer, Kernels

Part of Sarvam's Performance Engineering team. We are hiring two specialized performance roles - Kernels (this posting) and Inference (companion posting). They are a vertical stack: the kernels team authors the µs-level GPU code, and the inference team integrates it into a running serving stack and owns the system-level numbers. If your depth genuinely spans both, apply to either and tell us - but most candidates are strongest in one, and we hire for that depth.

Location: [Bengaluru / Chennai / Hybrid / On-site] · Team: Performance Engineering · Level: Senior

About the team

Sarvam serves multiple model families - small and large LLMs, Mixture-of-Experts, streaming Indic ASR, and multimodal - across a multi-node, multi-tenant fleet on H100 / H200 / B200. The Performance Engineering team owns the numbers the rest of the company plans against: how fast we serve, how much it costs, and how much we get out of every GPU. This team works at the intersection of the serving runtime, the kernel layer, and the SRE org that keeps the fleet alive.


About the role

You will own the kernel layer. Where stock libraries - cuBLAS, cuDNN, FlashAttention, out-of-the-box Triton - leave performance on the table, you will author the custom CUDA, DSL-based, and PTX kernels that close the gap.

This is a hard, narrow, high-leverage role. We hire engineers who have shipped kernels that beat published baselines on real workloads, not engineers who have used kernels. When your code lands, production p99 moves, and you own the explanation of why.

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years in ML systems, with 2+ years authoring production CUDA kernels. You have a kernel in production that beat the prior baseline by a measurable margin.

  • CUDA at kernel-authoring level: thread-block sizing, shared-memory layout, warp primitives, async copies (cp.async, TMA), and MMA selection.

  • CUTLASS / CuTe DSL at a modify-and-extend level, with comfort in the layout algebra.

  • PTX at a debug-and-modify level - you have inserted hand-written PTX where the compiler missed.

  • Nsight Compute and Systems fluency: you read a roofline plot and propose the fix.

  • Attention kernels: you have authored or modified at least one (FlashAttention-family, paged, MLA, sliding-window, or sparse).

  • Multi-architecture awareness: what changes from Hopper to Blackwell (TMA, WGMMA, tcgen05).


Strong pluses

  • Communication kernels - NCCL / NVSHMEM authoring, custom collectives, expert-parallel dispatch (DeepEP-style), AFD bipartite comms (StepMesh-style), KV transfer (DualPath / Mooncake). Strongly desired; dedicated comms-specialist headcount is expected later.

  • Open-source kernel contributions - FlashAttention, CUTLASS examples, vLLM / SGLang kernels, DeepEP, Mooncake, or non-trivial Triton work. For this role, the GitHub filter is the highest-yield signal.

  • tcgen05, TMA, CTA-cluster launch and distributed shared memory, async pipelining, and the FP4/microscaling paths

  • Grace-side host-path optimization on GH200 / GB200.

  • Source-level fluency in one of SGLang, vLLM, Dynamo, or TensorRT-LLM - you have modified the scheduler, the KV allocator, or the disaggregation path - and reading-level familiarity with the other three.

About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India’s full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India’s leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role

The Senior Manager, Growth Marketing owns how more of the right people discover Sarvam, try it, activate, and become long-term users.

This is an end-to-end growth role spanning acquisition, developer adoption, conversion, lifecycle, and experimentation. The mandate is to build growth engines that compound, across search, content, community, paid channels, product-led loops, and the product funnel itself.

The work is measured not by traffic or clicks, but by quality signups, successful API usage, retention, and revenue. This person works closely with Product, Developer Relations, Content, Sales, and Analytics to understand where growth is coming from, remove friction across the funnel, and continuously find new ways to scale adoption.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the growth funnel. Own the journey from discovery → signup → first successful API call → habitual usage → paid conversion → team expansion. Understand where users drop, instrument the funnel, and systematically improve it.

  • Drive acquisition. Grow high-quality acquisition across search, content, community, paid search, paid social, and new distribution channels. Build a balanced mix of channels that can scale efficiently over time.

  • Grow developer adoption. Increase API usage and open-weight model adoption. Work closely with Product and DevRel on documentation, technical content, developer journeys, and product-led growth loops.

  • Own search and discoverability. Build Sarvam's presence across traditional search, technical SEO, documentation SEO, and increasingly, AI-powered search and LLM answers.

  • Improve activation and onboarding. Reduce the time between signup and first value. Design onboarding, lifecycle communication, product nudges, and experiments that help developers get to a successful first use case quickly.

  • Drive conversion. Continuously improve landing pages, signup flows, pricing journeys, paywalls, and other conversion points that turn interest into usage and usage into revenue.

  • Build retention and expansion loops. Identify the behaviours that predict long-term usage, churn, and account growth. Build lifecycle, re-engagement, retargeting, and product interventions around them.

  • Run experimentation. Maintain a continuous backlog of growth experiments across acquisition, activation, conversion, and retention. Ship quickly, measure rigorously, and scale what works.

  • Own growth economics. Understand acquisition efficiency across channels and cohorts. Own CAC, payback, LTV, attribution, and budget allocation, with a clear view of where the next incremental unit of growth should come from.

  • Analytics and instrumentation. Define the metrics the growth team runs on, ensure the right events and funnels are instrumented, and build dashboards that make performance visible and actionable.

  • Build AI-native workflows. Use AI across research, content, creative, SEO, targeting, experimentation, and analysis to compress cycles and operate a highly leveraged growth motion.

Requirements

  • 7–10 years of experience in growth marketing, with hands-on ownership of a PLG or self-serve funnel

  • Track record of growing acquisition, activation, conversion, and revenue with quantified outcomes

  • Strong hands-on understanding of both search/discoverability and paid acquisition

  • Experience building content, community, SEO, or product-led growth loops that drove meaningful adoption

  • Strong experimentation discipline; able to design, run, analyse, and act on experiments rigorously

  • Comfort with analytics and instrumentation; able to define metrics, pull data, diagnose funnels, and understand CAC, payback, and LTV

  • Experience marketing to developers or technical buyers

  • Comfortable operating across both product and marketing surfaces rather than treating growth as a channel function

  • Fluent in modern AI tools across research, creative, content, analytics, and growth workflows

Good to Have

  • Experience growing an API, SDK, developer product, or open-weight/open-source model

  • Deep familiarity with SEO, AI-powered search, and LLM discoverability

  • Experience with lifecycle, retention, and conversion-rate optimisation

  • Experience building a growth motion from scratch at a founder-led or early-stage company

  • Familiarity with a self-serve developer motion and an enterprise sales motion running side by side

  • Experience managing or mentoring growth, lifecycle, SEO, content, performance, or analytics contributors

Why Sarvam?

Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems that push the frontiers of AI with real population-scale impact.

  • Work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar

  • High ownership and high impact, from day one

  • Everything we do is AI-first, from the way we build and ship to the way we think about problems

  • You can work on problems that could change how an entire country learns, works, and communicates

If you want to work on problems at the frontier of AI in India, Sarvam is the place to be.

About the Role

This role sits at the intersection of customer success, technical problem-solving, and market intelligence. You’ll own API customer relationships end-to-end — running demos, debugging integrations, writing scripts to unblock customers, and relaying precise model feedback to Sarvam’s research teams. A strong fit for someone early in their career with genuine technical curiosity and excellent communication skills.

 

What You’ll Do

• Own customer relationships end-to-end: run demos, onboarding sessions, and integration walkthroughs; get customers from API key to working product fast; stay with them through production.

• Build and tinker: write scripts to unblock integrations, build small demo apps that show customers what’s possible, and create reference implementations others can reuse. Handle problems directly rather than escalating them.

• Be the voice of the customer inside Sarvam: relay model feedback (transcription errors, voice quality gaps, translation failures, LLM output issues) to research and engineering with enough specificity that they can reproduce and prioritise; then close the loop with the customer.

• Surface market insights: track what customers and prospects are building, map the competitive landscape, spot recurring patterns across accounts, and bring a point of view to GTM and Product — not just a data dump.

 

What We’re Looking For

• 3+ years in a customer-facing role: customer success, solutions, pre-sales, or developer advocacy at a tech company; strong internship experience counts (impact > years).

• Technically capable: you read API docs fluently, write basic Python or JS scripts, and debug integrations without hand-holding.

• Excellent communicator: confident on demos, clear in writing, equally effective with a business stakeholder and an engineer.

• Genuinely curious about AI: you want to understand how the models work, not just what they return, and you can characterise model errors with precision.

• Organised and proactive: multiple threads in the air, nothing dropped, no prompting needed.

 

Bonus Points

• Familiarity with speech, LLM, or document processing APIs: you know what good output looks like.

• Experience working with engineering or research teams: you can turn a customer complaint into a reproducible bug report.

• You’ve built something with an API — a project, a side build, anything.

 

Why Sarvam?

Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems that push the frontiers of AI with real population-scale impact.

• Work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar.

• High ownership and high impact, from day one.

• Everything we do is AI-first, from the way we build and ship to the way we think about problems.

• You can work on problems that could change how an entire country learns, works, and communicates.

If you want to work on problems at the frontier of AI in India, Sarvam is the place to be.

About team:

Chanakya is Sarvam AI's specialised, self-contained vertical for national security and institutions of national importance. It carries its own pricing, business, product, engineering, custom-model and vendor functions under one roof — a complete unit built to solve the most complex problems in the strategic sector: the three armed forces, intelligence agencies, financial regulators, and institutions of national importance such as central ministries and national policy bodies.

What we deploy here must be at strategic parity or higher — anything less is a national-security risk. That standard is the reason Chanakya is a small, exceptionally high-performing team inside Sarvam, and the reason we are deliberate about who joins it.

Why this is one of the most consequential seats in Indian AI

01 — NATIONAL IMPACT

You sit where it all gets decided.

These systems are deployed inside the institutions that safeguard the country. The potential for national impact is not abstract — it is at the core of how the strategic sector reasons, decides, and acts. Few roles anywhere in Indian technology carry this weight.

02 — UNPARALLELED LEARNING

Full-stack, end to end — nowhere else does this exist.

Every deployment runs the entire stack: understanding a customer's real requirement, architecting and customising the stack for it, and where needed building and fine-tuning models, shaping training data, and inventing data representations for extraordinarily complex data, workflows and applications. You touch nearly the whole arc of the work. This experience sets you apart — whether you go on to found a company, or become a business or technology leader in the years ahead, at Sarvam or beyond.

03 — A PATH TO LEADERSHIP

These are leadership seats in the making.

Chanakya's functions are being built out now. We are looking for people who will grow into the leaders of these emerging functions — every one of these roles is a route to leading a part of the vertical, not just filling it.

Where we are. This is not a leap into the unknown. Chanakya has already achieved product–market fit to a meaningful degree, has significant revenue booked, and has large strategic projects officially underway. Things are structured and going well.

The opportunity. This is a genuine zero-to-one journey — but one taken within the reach, talent and standing of a company like Sarvam. You get the ambition and ownership of building something new, backed by the full weight of Sarvam's capability and presence. The golden opportunity: to help build out and lead the emerging functions of Chanakya, with a clear growth path ahead.

Where client-facing instinct meets technical depth — working directly with the founders.

You will bring your client-facing judgement and technical fluency together to shape and drive Chanakya's go-to-market, working closely with the leadership and the founders to get it built.

•Strong technical foundation plus sharp commercial and strategic instincts.

•Comfortable in the room with senior institutional stakeholders and with our own engineers.

•Entrepreneurial temperament — owns outcomes end to end.

The bar.

Across every one of these roles, we are looking for people who want to change the world and build something of national consequence — and who will grow into the leaders of Chanakya's verticals. If that is you, the ceiling here is set only by your ambition.

Base: Delhi NCR, with travel across India. All roles involve working inside restricted environments and travelling to client sites at short notice.

About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India’s full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India’s leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role

Sarvam’s brand is already an argument about motion — it just hasn’t been allowed to move yet.

The monogram is a gateway that emerges — layered circles resolving out of mandala geometry into a single threshold form. The palette isn’t a set of swatches; it’s a continuous run from blue to orange, built to suggest progression and responsive state. Both of those ideas are about change over time. Both are currently being made mostly in stills.

We want the person who resolves that. Not someone to animate a logo once for a launch, but someone who decides how this brand behaves — how it enters, how it responds, how a gradient moves without becoming wallpaper — and then builds that language across films, web and product.

It’s a rare brief: a real identity with real motion logic baked into it, and nobody has run at it yet.

What you’ll do

  • Define the motion language, not just the motion. Timing, easing, entrances, transitions, how the monogram behaves and how the gradient travels — documented and reusable, so the next fifty assets don’t start from zero.

  • Make the films. Model launches, product announcements, research drops, event opens, brand pieces. Concept, board, animate, edit, sound, deliver — you’ll own the shot end to end.

  • Make the product move too. Web animation, scroll behaviour, UI micro-interactions, demo and walkthrough videos. This is the half of the role that keeps the other half honest: motion that ships inside a live surface has constraints a film doesn’t.

  • Hand off cleanly to engineering. Lottie, Rive, sprite sequences, or a spec an engineer can actually build from. Work that dies in After Effects doesn’t count.

  • Solve the hard one: visualising speech. Our products are conversational — voice agents across 11 Indian languages, code-switching mid-sentence. Showing listening, thinking, speaking and switching, without falling back on a generic waveform, is the most interesting motion problem in the building.

  • Use AI properly in the pipeline. Generative video, boards and previz, roto, upscaling, variation. You should already be doing this, with a clear sense of where it saves a week and where it costs you the shot.

  • Work across the whole company. Design, marketing, product, research, founders. Rough briefs, hard launch dates, and work that still holds up at the end of it.

What we’re looking for

  • 3+ years in motion design, in-house or at a studio, with a reel that shows both narrative work and work that shipped inside a product or website.

  • Deep After Effects. Shape layers, expressions, proper rigging — not template-and-swap. Plus real editing chops in Premiere or Resolve.

  • Figma is non-negotiable. Motion here starts inside the design system, not beside it.

  • Illustrator and Photoshop at working depth — you’ll be building and cleaning your own assets.

  • Fundamentals over flourish. Timing, weight, staging, anticipation, and how type behaves in motion. We will notice your easing curves.

  • Native fluency with AI tools in a professional motion workflow, and a point of view about it.

  • System thinking. Evidence you’ve taken a static identity and extended it into motion — or taken a motion system somewhere its guidelines hadn’t gone.

  • A real stake in this. You should care specifically about what Indian design deserves to look like in motion — and be a little impatient that it mostly doesn’t look like that yet.

Bonus points

  • 3D — Blender or Cinema 4D, especially for abstract systems, geometry and product visualisation

  • Real-time or code-based motion: Rive, three.js, GLSL, TouchDesigner, Houdini

  • Sound design and mix — or at least strong instincts about audio driving picture

  • Indic typography in motion: animating Devanagari, Tamil or Kannada without breaking the letterforms

 

How to apply

Send a reel — 90 seconds is plenty — plus a breakdown of what you did on each piece. Three shots you own completely beat a beautifully cut reel of team work. If one of them had to survive a real constraint — an engineer, a file size, a deadline, a language you don’t read — lead with that.

  • High ownership and high impact, from day one

About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India's full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC and LIC.


About the role

Sarvam's model APIs (ASR, TTS, Vision, LLM, Translate) are how developers and enterprises ship products on our foundation models. The platform handles tens of millions of API calls every day, over HTTP and WebSockets, with metering, billing, prepaid wallets and rate-limiting all part of the same stack.

We are hiring a Software Engineer to own major parts of this platform end to end, working closely with the Staff Engineer who leads its architecture. You will take an area such as speech to text pipeline,or text to speech pipeline, and be accountable for its reliability, performance and end-to-end latencies. This role is for someone who is obsessed with latencies, optimizes services and network paths to shave off milliseconds, ships fast, reasons from first principles, and treats AI as the default way to get engineering work done.


What you will do


Own a platform area end to end

• Own one or more major parts of the platform, such as the WebSocket streaming layer, a speech recognition pipeline, or text to speech pipeline: build, operate and improve them.

• Turn loosely defined goals into RFCs, milestones and shipped results, and write down the decisions and trade-offs.

• Be accountable after launch: on-call, incident response, root-cause analysis and follow-through on fixes.

• Make the call when a decision is needed, and own the outcome.

• Obsessed with latencies, dissecting existing services to understand the system, and tuning the right knobs to optimize performance.

• Bring services across without regressions in customer-facing APIs, latency or reliability.


Build real-time and model-serving pipelines

• Build and operate streaming infrastructure: WebSocket connections, long-lived sessions queue-based batch processing, backpressure and low-latency model invocation.

• Engineer audio pipelines: TTS chunking around model context limits, sample-rate conversion and format encoding, and VAD-based silence detection for ASR.

• Hold your services to sub-100ms latency SLOs in a multi-tenant environment, and know where every millisecond goes.


Think in systems and from first principles

• Reasons from constraints: latency budgets per hop, throughput, cost per request, failure modes and tenant isolation.

• Use back-of-the-envelope estimates to decide what to build, what to optimize and what to leave alone.

• Prefer simple designs you can fully explain over clever ones you cannot.

• Build in observability from day one: logging, metrics and tracing that let anyone debug production quickly.


Raise the bar for the team

• Strengthen the integration testing harness so the team can ship fast without breaking customer-facing APIs.

• Partner with the Inference and MLOps teams on making model serving fast, reliable and operable.

• Mentor junior engineers through RFC reviews, code review and pairing.

• Practice design-first, documentation-first engineering: RFCs before code, no tribal knowledge.


What we are looking for

• 4–6 years of building and operating production backend systems.

• At least one service you owned end to end under real load, including what broke and what you changed.

• Strong distributed-systems fundamentals: concurrency, networking, queues, caching, consistency and failure modes.

• Experience with low-latency or high-throughput services, and comfort reasoning about p95 and p99 latency.

• Solid fundamentals with a relational database and a cache, such as PostgreSQL and Redis: schema design, query performance and caching strategy.

• Fluency in at least one backend language and willingness to work in both Python and Golang.

• Experience running services with containers, CI/CD and production monitoring.

• Daily, hands-on use of AI tools in your engineering workflow, with concrete examples of what you automated or sped up.

• A bias for action: fast on reversible decisions, careful on irreversible ones.

• Clear writing, especially RFCs and design docs that others can act on.


Good to have (not required)

• Voice AI or real-time audio experience: WebSockets, WebRTC, streaming ASR or TTS, or audio processing with FFmpeg or pyav, codecs, sample rates and VAD.

• Production experience in Go, or in Python with FastAPI.

• Experience serving LLM, ASR, TTS or vision models in production.

• Experience building metering, billing, wallet or payments infrastructure.

• Running services on Kubernetes in production.

• Time at an early- or growth-stage startup.


Why Sarvam

• A fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, with real population-scale impact.

• Researchers, engineers, builders and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar.

• High ownership and high impact from day one.

• AI-first in everything, from how we build and ship to how we think about problems
