Enterprises want agents that can do real work on their own data. That data sits across documents, databases and business systems that were never built for agents to read, and today's agents forget most of what they learn once a session ends.

Our team builds Sarvam's context engine to solve both problems. The knowledge side brings an enterprise's data together so agents can search it, navigate it and cite where an answer came from. The memory side lets agents remember what they learn over time, about individual users, about teams, and across the organisation. We want both to keep improving as they are used.

Knowledge and memory for agents is a rapidly evolving field. We want to build at the frontier of it, and to show with measurable results that our approach does better than traditional ones.


About Sarvam

Sarvam is India's leading full-stack AI company, building sovereign AI infrastructure and applications purpose-built for India. Headquartered in Bengaluru and founded by leading AI researchers, Sarvam builds foundational models for Indian languages, enterprise AI platforms, and voice-first AI agents that serve hundreds of millions of Indians. Sarvam is backed by top-tier investors and works with national and state governments, large enterprises, and developers across the country. We are building the AI layer for a billion people.


What this role promises you

You will join a small team and own large parts of the platform. The work is driven by real customer deployments, so what you build gets used quickly and you see what works and what does not. You will also work closely with the teams building Sarvam's models, document AI and inference, which makes it much easier to solve problems that cut across the stack.


What you'll do

  • Build and run the ingestion pipeline that parses, extracts and indexes large volumes of documents, and keep it reliable when files are messy and external services fail.

  • Connect to databases and enterprise systems so agents can work with structured records as well as documents.

  • Design how enterprise data is modelled, including the ontology, matching the same entity across sources, and tracing every value back to where it came from.

  • Build the retrieval tools agents call, with search, filters and citations, and make them fast and cheap enough for agents to use heavily.

  • Build memory for agents at the level of a user, a team and the whole organisation: how it is written, stored, retrieved and kept accurate over time.

  • Run evals, find where answers go wrong, and keep iterating until quality improves.

  • Work with product and forward-deployed engineers to turn what one customer needs into something the platform does for every customer.

  • Write design docs and keep decisions documented.

Our production stack is Go, with Temporal, OpenSearch and Postgres.


Who you are

We are hiring at 3 to 5 years of experience.

  • You have built and run backend or data systems in production, and you have fixed them when they broke.

  • You are strong in at least one backend language. Our core is in Go, so Go experience is a plus, and you should be happy to work in it every day.

  • You have good fundamentals in data modelling and PostgreSQL.

  • You have worked on long-running pipelines and know how to make them safe to retry and recover.

  • You have worked on search or retrieval and know how to debug why the right result did not come back.

  • You use AI coding tools every day and have a good sense of where they help and where they don't.

  • You care about measuring quality, and you are comfortable building the evals to do it.

Bonus points

  • Experience with knowledge graphs, ontologies, entity resolution or structured extraction.

  • Experience building memory for agents or LLM applications.

  • Document processing, such as OCR, layout or table extraction.

  • Connectors or change data capture for ERP, CRM or other enterprise systems.

  • Building on MCP, or serving LLMs and embedding models in production.

  • On-prem or air-gapped deployments.

  • Experience at an early- or growth-stage startup.

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India, a full-stack sovereign AI platform spanning research, models, infrastructure, and applications, with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. About the Role

We are looking for a sharp, high-ownership Marketing Intern to act as the primary story-builder and content engine across Sarvam’s marketing channels.

This is not a passive internship focused on surface-level social updates. You will translate complex frontier AI capabilities like our Vision APIs, Document Intelligence models, and voice platforms into crisp, high-impact stories, viral launch threads, and sharp enterprise collateral. You will sit at the intersection of product, creative execution, and creator operations, helping shape how Sarvam communicates its sovereign AI vision to technical builders, enterprise buyers, and the broader ecosystem.

What You'll Do

Customer Stories & Launch Comms

  • Transform technical milestones into narratives: Turn enterprise customer deployments into compelling case studies and written success stories.

  • Drive product launch comms: Draft multi-channel launch content—from sharp X/LinkedIn feature threads to enterprise mailers for prospects and existing clients.

  • Simplify the complex: Translate technical AI concepts into clear, punchy prose without losing accuracy or depth.

Social Content & Video Operations

  • Drive video execution: Write scripts for explainer videos and product walkthroughs; coordinate shoots and post-production workflows.

  • Manage multi-platform publishing: Oversee daily social presence across X, LinkedIn, Instagram, and YouTube, ensuring high content velocity and visual quality.

Creator & Influencer Operations

  • Manage creator partnerships: Source, pitch, and recruit relevant tech creators, developer voices, and industry influencers.

  • Execute campaign logistics: Draft campaign briefs, align timelines, and track deliverables from initial outreach to final publish.

What We're Looking For

  • Editorial precision: Exceptional written English skills with an instinct for tone, structure, and clarity across social, email, and long-form formats.

  • Technical translation capability: Comfortable diving into technical platforms, developer dashboards, or AI research to write simple, accurate marketing copy.

  • AI-first workflow: Habitual use of AI tools for rapid research, content structuring, and drafting.

  • Platform fluency: Deep, native understanding of content formats, algorithms, and tone across X, LinkedIn, Instagram, and YouTube.

  • Execution & ownership: Uncompromising attention to detail, strong organizational discipline, and the ability to drive multiple deadlines without hand-holding.

Bonus Points

  • Hands-on experience with video editing tools or basic script-to-edit workflows.

  • Familiarity with design tools (Canva, Figma) to quickly mock up assets or social creatives.

  • Prior experience managing creator outreach, influencer pipelines, or talent operations.

  • Vernacular fluency in Hindi or a regional Indian language.

  • Foundational understanding of SEO best practices for written content.

Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems at the frontier of AI with population-scale impact. High ownership and high impact from day one, AI-first in everything we do, on problems that could change how an entire country works and communicates.

About the team

Sarvam builds Indic-language AI used at population scale. The CPU Infrastructure team runs everything outside the GPU fleet: Kubernetes across Azure, AWS, GCP and Indian sovereign clouds, the network between them, Cloudflare, identity, secrets, observability, cost and the delivery pipeline every product ships through.

The team builds and runs what it builds. Engineers own real systems end to end, and every repeated piece of manual work is a candidate for automation. As an AI company, we are building AI agents into our own operations, to plan and review infrastructure changes, triage alerts and handle routine issues, with engineers setting the guardrails.

About the role

You are an infrastructure engineer whose first instinct is security, and who builds rather than only operates. You have worked on banking, fintech, payments or similarly regulated products, where a misconfiguration is an incident and an audit is routine. Here you set what “secure” means across Sarvam’s infrastructure and build the automation that enforces it, so security is a property of the pipeline rather than a review step. You work closely with the compliance team.

This is a hands-on role: most of your time goes into building, and you guide engineering teams across Sarvam on security — setting standards, reviewing security-relevant work and mentoring engineers.

Responsibilities

• Define and enforce security baselines for Kubernetes, cloud accounts, container images and CI/CD across all clouds

• Write the policy gates in the delivery pipeline (OPA / Conftest, Kyverno or equivalent): network exposure, IAM, image provenance, secrets, data residency

• Own secrets and workload identity: Vault or cloud-native equivalents, rotation, short-lived and scoped credentials, no long-lived keys

• Build detection and response: runtime security (Falco / Tetragon or equivalent), log-based detections, alerting and playbooks

• Run the finding-to-fix loop for security findings: triage, assign, fix, add a detection, retest

• Use LLMs and AI agents in security work: triaging findings, reviewing infrastructure changes, tuning detections, drafting incident timelines — and secure the agents themselves with scoped, short-lived permissions and audit trails

• Harden the supply chain: image signing and scanning, dependency policy, SBOMs

• Automate compliance evidence (CERT-In, ISO 27001, SOC 2, DPDP) together with the compliance team

• Set the security standards other engineers follow and review security-relevant changes

• Take part in on-call and lead security incidents

Requirements

• 5–9 years in DevOps, platform or security engineering, with at least 2 in a bank, fintech, payments company or other regulated environment

• Strong Kubernetes and Linux fundamentals; has run production clusters on at least one major cloud

• Hands-on with Terraform / OpenTofu and GitOps (ArgoCD or Flux)

• Has built security automation, not only operated tools: policy-as-code, secrets rotation, CI/CD security gates or detection pipelines

• Working knowledge of IAM, network security, TLS and secrets management across clouds

• Scripting and tooling in Python or Go

• Has been through security audits and knows what evidence auditors need

• Has built or used AI-based automation in infrastructure or security work, and understands the risks of AI agents: prompt injection, over-broad permissions, unreviewed actions

• Nice to have: Vault, SPIFFE / SPIRE, Falco or Tetragon, Cloudflare WAF, incident response lead experience, multi-cloud experience

About the Role

Sarvam's model APIs (LLM, ASR, TTS, Vision, Translate) are how developers and enterprises ship products on our foundation models. Our OpenAI-compatible LLM APIs route every request across multiple model deployments, with streaming, failover, metering, billing, and rate-limiting all part of the same stack. Today it's FastAPI and Python; we're in the middle of rewriting it in Go.

We're hiring a Software Engineer (SDE 2) to own core parts of this platform. The features. The reliability. The performance. This is an IC role.


What You'll Do

  • Building and evolving the LLM API platform, from the moment a request hits the edge to the response that goes back out

  • The Python→Go rewrite: building services in Go alongside the existing Python stack, without compromising reliability

  • Streaming infrastructure: SSE for Chat Completions and Responses, long-lived connections, clean handling of cancellations and client disconnects

  • Routing and failover: weighted provider chains, retries with backoff, and latency-driven admission control across model deployments

  • Protocol compatibility: keeping the API faithful to the OpenAI spec across inference servers (vLLM, SGLang, Dynamo) that each behave slightly differently

  • The commercial layer: metering, billing, and rate-limiting, engineered to the same bar as the model APIs themselves

  • Performance and reliability for a multi-tenant platform serving long-context agentic and coding workloads

  • Observability (logging, metrics, tracing), so the team can debug production confidently and quickly

  • Integration and load testing: the harness that lets us ship fast without breaking customer-facing APIs

  • Close partnership with the Inference and MLOps teams on production readiness for new model launches

  • Design-first, documentation-first engineering culture within the team: RFCs before code, decisions written down, no tribal knowledge


What We're Looking For

  • 3+ years building production backend systems

  • Strong Python in production: asyncio, FastAPI or similar, and services you've built and operated under real load

  • Working knowledge of Go, or a strong willingness to learn it: you'll work in both languages through the rewrite

  • Experience building low-latency, multi-tenant backend services

  • Hands-on experience with streaming systems: SSE or WebSockets, long-lived connections, backpressure

  • Strong PostgreSQL and Redis fundamentals: schema design, query performance, caching, and rate limiting

  • Comfort running services on Kubernetes in production

  • An ownership mindset: you test before you ship, debug production with metrics, logs, and traces, and write the RCA afterwards


Bonus Points

  • Experience serving or integrating LLMs in production, especially OpenAI-compatible APIs

  • Familiarity with inference servers (vLLM, SGLang, Dynamo) and latency metrics such as time to first token and inter-token latency

  • Experience building metering, billing, or usage-based pricing infrastructure

  • Time at an early- or growth-stage startup: comfort with ambiguity, speed, and ownership


Why Sarvam?

Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems that push the frontiers of AI with real population-scale impact.

  • Work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar

  • High ownership and high impact, from day one

  • Everything we do is AI-first, from the way we build and ship to the way we think about problems

  • You can work on problems that could change how an entire country learns, works, and communicates

If you want to work on problems at the frontier of AI in India, Sarvam is the place to be.

About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India's full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam partners with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role

We’re looking for a technical writer to help people understand what we’re building, how it works and what they can do with it.

You’ll work closely with researchers, engineers and product teams to write about the decisions, advances and practical applications behind our work. That could mean explaining how we train a model, developing the story for a product launch or showing developers how to build with our APIs.

The role calls for technical curiosity and strong editorial judgement. You should enjoy getting into the details, asking questions until you understand something and finding a clear, compelling way to explain it. You’ll have substantial ownership over what we publish and how we sound.

What you’ll do

  • Write research papers, engineering blogs, product announcements and technical deep dives across Sarvam’s models and products.

  • Work directly with researchers and engineers to understand their work, draw out interesting ideas and develop pieces from early conversations through publication.

  • Explain technical approaches, benchmark results and design decisions with enough detail for readers to understand the evidence and trade-offs.

  • Develop launch narratives that clearly articulate what a model or product does, what has improved and where it is useful.

  • Adapt ideas across formats, from a detailed technical article to a product page, launch email or short social post.

  • Edit contributions from technical teams, strengthening their structure and readability while preserving the author’s expertise and intent.

  • Own fact checking, technical reviews and revisions, and help establish consistent editorial standards across our published work.

What you’ll bring

  • A portfolio of published work that demonstrates clear thinking, strong writing and the ability to explain technical subjects.

  • Enough familiarity with AI and software to read technical material, follow an engineering discussion and ask informed questions.

  • Strong judgement about structure, voice and detail. You can find the central idea in a complex subject and build a piece around it.

  • The ability to write for developers and researchers, as well as readers encountering a subject for the first time.

  • Care with evidence and claims. You know when a statement needs a source, a qualification or another conversation with the team.

  • Experience working with subject experts and incorporating feedback while keeping a piece coherent.

  • The initiative to identify stories worth telling and the discipline to bring them through to publication.

Experience that would help

You may have worked as a technical writer, technology journalist, developer educator or editor at a technology company or research organisation. Experience with AI models, APIs, developer tools or infrastructure would be useful, as would the ability to try products and run simple code examples yourself.

About Sarvam AI

Sarvam AI is building India's sovereign AI stack, spanning foundational models, infrastructure and applications. Our mission is to make powerful AI accessible and useful for India, building technology that works across languages, industries and real-world use cases.

As we continue to build and scale our products, understanding how people interact with them becomes increasingly important. We're looking for a curious and research-oriented intern to help us understand our users better and shape the experiences we build.

The Role

As a Product User Research Intern, you'll work closely with our product, design and engineering teams to understand user behaviour, identify friction points and uncover opportunities to improve our products.

You'll interact directly with developers, product managers and founders, study how they use Sarvam's products, and translate your findings into actionable insights that influence product and design decisions.

This is an opportunity to work on a new user research function at Sarvam, helping establish research practices and processes from the ground up. You'll also get ownership of a primary product area and the opportunity to see your research translate into real product improvements.

What You'll Work On

  • Understand our users: Conduct user interviews, surveys and usability studies with developers, PMs and founders to understand their needs, behaviours and challenges.

  • Improve product experiences: Research user journeys across Sarvam's developer console, playground, API documentation and applications. Identify friction points across onboarding, API key creation, first API calls, billing and other key workflows.

  • Study developer journeys: Analyse the developer funnel, from sign-up to making the first API call and eventually becoming a paying user. Understand where users drop off and, more importantly, why.

  • Test and evaluate designs: Conduct usability testing on existing interfaces and new prototypes, run preference and A/B tests, and benchmark experiences against other developer products.

  • Turn research into insights: Analyse qualitative and quantitative data, identify patterns and present clear recommendations to product, design, growth and support teams.

  • Build the research practice: Help establish research playbooks, interview templates, participant recruitment processes and a research repository that can scale with the team.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong curiosity about user behaviour and a genuine interest in understanding why people use products the way they do.

  • Comfortable speaking with users, conducting interviews and asking thoughtful, unbiased questions.

  • Technical fluency — you should be comfortable reading API documentation, making basic API calls using tools like Postman, curl or Python, and understanding what might have gone wrong when an API fails.

  • Comfortable working with data, analysing spreadsheets and interpreting product funnels or dashboards.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate research findings into clear insights and recommendations.

  • Familiarity with AI tools and developer products, and an interest in exploring how they can improve research workflows.

Good to Have

  • Experience with SQL or product analytics tools such as Mixpanel, Amplitude or Metabase.

  • Familiarity with user research methodologies, usability testing and survey design.

  • Experience reviewing Figma prototypes or conducting user interviews.

  • Previous research projects, internships or personal projects involving products you've built or shipped.

  • Fluency in one or more Indian languages.

Who Can Apply?

  • Final-year students or graduates who have completed their studies within the last 12 months.

  • Candidates from engineering, psychology, economics, design or social science backgrounds.

  • Individuals who can commit to a full-time, 6-month, in-office internship in Bengaluru.

What You'll Get

  • The opportunity to help build Sarvam's user research function from the ground up.

  • Direct exposure to product, design and engineering teams working on India's sovereign AI ecosystem.

  • Hands-on experience researching developer products and real-world AI applications.

  • Ownership of meaningful research projects with findings that directly influence product decisions.

  • An opportunity to work closely with experienced product leaders and learn how research translates into better products.

  • Potential for a pre-placement offer (PPO) based on performance.

About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of sovereign AI for India. We are developing India's full-stack AI platform across research, models, infrastructure and applications, with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India: in Indian languages, on Indian data and at Indian scale.

Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC and LIC, alongside central and state governments. Sarvam is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV and Khosla Ventures.

About the Role

AI is moving quickly from demos to real-world applications, and making that transition work is no small task.

As a Deployment Strategist I at Sarvam, you'll work at the intersection of business, technology and AI. From understanding how a bank operates to figuring out how an AI agent can improve its customer experience, you'll be involved in solving problems that don't always come with ready-made answers.

You'll work closely with clients and our Engineering and Product teams to identify opportunities, build prototypes and take solutions towards production. Expect a mix of business conversations, problem-solving, data, technology and plenty of hands-on execution.

We are hiring across locations: Mumbai - for BFSI, industrials, manufacturing | Delhi - industrials, manufacturing, government | Bangalore - Digital native

What You'll Do

  • Work with enterprise and government clients to understand their workflows, challenges and identify where AI can create value.

  • Break down business problems into clear requirements, use cases and actionable solutions.

  • Build prototypes and proof-of-concepts using Python, APIs and LLM-based tools to test ideas and demonstrate what's possible.

  • Work closely with Engineering and Product teams to take solutions from initial concepts to production.

  • Analyse data, track adoption and measure how deployed solutions are performing.

  • Own individual workstreams, coordinate with stakeholders and keep deployments moving.

  • Bring client feedback and learnings back to the team to improve our products and deployment approaches.

What We're Looking For

  • 2–4 years of experience in consulting, product, engineering, business strategy or customer-facing technology roles.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to bring structure to ambiguous problems.

  • Good understanding of business processes and an interest in applying AI to solve practical problems.

  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work across business and technical teams.

  • A bias for action, curiosity and a strong sense of ownership.

Good to Have

  • Exposure to LLMs, AI agents or GenAI applications.

  • Experience working with enterprise clients, particularly in BFSI, manufacturing or government.

  • Proficiency in Hindi or other Indian regional languages.

  • Engineering undergraduate degree.

  • Prior work experience in core engineering roles.

  • MBA or postgraduate qualification from a reputed institution.

Why Sarvam?

Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems that push the frontiers of AI with real population-scale impact.

  • Work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar

  • High ownership and high impact, from day one

  • Everything we do is AI-first, from the way we build and ship to the way we think about problems

  • You can work on problems that could change how an entire country learns, works, and communicates

If you want to work on problems at the frontier of AI in India, Sarvam is the place to be.

About the role

We're hiring two backend-heavy full-stack engineers (SDE 2 or SDE 3) for the Cowork team at Sarvam. Cowork is the agentic side of Indus: users hand it real work, and an agent plans, uses tools and connectors, works in a cloud sandbox, and hands back files, docs and artifacts across web, Android, iOS, macOS and Windows.

The role is full stack, but the centre of gravity is the backend: the BFF that every client talks to, and increasingly the agent harness behind it. You'll ship features end to end, from the API and data model through to the client screens on mobile, desktop and web.

What you'll work on

Most of your time goes into the BFF and the services around it; the rest into client work and the harness, depending on what the roadmap needs that quarter.

  • BFF (Chat Service): design and own the APIs that web, mobile and desktop share: sessions, conversations, streaming turns, artifacts, connectors, custom and managed agents. Data modelling, migrations, auth and RBAC, pagination and search.

  • Real-time streaming: stream LLM output, tool calls and agent events from the harness to clients over an event bus, and keep it correct under reconnects, retries and partial failures.

  • Agent harness and platform: contribute to Panja, our agent harness: tool and MCP integrations, sandboxed execution, file and artifact flows, latency and token-cost work.

  • Clients: build features end to end on our Kotlin/Compose Multiplatform apps (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows) and the Next.js web app, so a feature you design in the backend reaches users on every surface.

  • Production ownership: observability, on-call, RCAs, and making the system faster and cheaper with numbers to back it.


Tech stack

Python and PostgreSQL are the core; you don't need every item below on day one.

  • Backend: Python, SQLAlchemy + Alembic, PostgreSQL, OpenAPI

  • Supporting services: Go

  • Mobile and desktop: Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows)

  • Web: Next.js, React, TypeScript


What we're looking for

A strong backend engineer who has also shipped real frontend work and is happy to keep doing both.

  • 3+ years (SDE 2) or 5+ years (SDE 3) building and running production backend services.

  • Deep in at least one backend language; Python preferred, Go, Kotlin/JVM or TypeScript/Node also welcome.

  • Solid API and data-model design: REST/streaming APIs, PostgreSQL schema design, migrations, indexing, transactions.

  • Distributed-systems fundamentals: async processing, queues or event streams, idempotency, retries, failure handling.

  • Production experience on Kubernetes or a similar platform, with observability you actually used to debug an incident.

  • Has shipped user-facing features on at least one client platform: Android, iOS, desktop or web (React/Next.js). Kotlin/Compose experience is a plus, not a gate.

  • Willing to pick up the side of the stack they know less, and to learn agent and LLM systems on the job.

  • Clear written communication: design docs, PR descriptions, RCAs.

Nice to have

  • Built on LLM APIs: tool calling, streaming, prompt caching, evals, or an agent loop of your own.

  • MCP servers or clients, OAuth connector integrations, or sandboxed code execution.

  • Kotlin Multiplatform / Compose Multiplatform, or native Android/iOS.

  • Real-time systems: WebSockets/SSE, NATS, Kafka, or Temporal-style durable workflows.

  • Go services, or performance and cost work with measurable before/after numbers.

  • Open-source work or public writing we can read.
